# The Student Founder

> The Student Founder: Why Your Student Years Are the Best Time to Build Something Real. A book by Andrew Ashur, founder and CEO of Lucid Bots. Tagline: "$42 in the bank. No permission slip." Core sentence: "As a student, trying is free. After graduation, it's the most expensive thing you'll ever buy."

The book is a practical manual for high school students, college students, and recent graduates who want to build something real while trying still costs almost nothing. Its argument: what stands between a student and a first paying customer is not experience. Experience has a substitute, and the substitute is agency, which the book measures as the Agency Quotient, the number of days between having an idea nobody assigned you and taking one concrete action on it.

Status: manuscript complete, advance reader's copy exists, publication February 2027. Readers can leave an email at https://www.thestudentfounder.com to be notified at launch.

## Pages

- [Home](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/): the book, the Agency Quotient question, the Founder's Page, author bio, FAQ, and launch-list signup.
- [Press kit](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/press.html): book facts, bios, images, lines from the book, interview topics, and contact.
- [Prologue: Blood in the Shoes](https://www.thestudentfounder.com/prologue.html): the full prologue, free. The two-mile walk across Chicago with $42 in the company account and the investor on the twenty-eighth floor who said yes.

## Contents of the book

- The Odds: what happens to founders who lose, told by two of them by name.
- Finding your idea: a real problem, not one that only sounds good. Compliments are not currency. Money is the truth.
- Finding the time: you don't have a time problem, you have a priority problem.
- Customers before product: an hour with a customer beats eight hours at a desk.
- Building it: it doesn't need to be pretty, it needs to exist.
- The 30-day sprint: the whole book compressed into thirty days of reps.
- The Founder's Page: ten blank lines about the reader's own problem, filled in one per chapter.

## Author

Andrew Ashur is the founder and CEO of Lucid Bots, which builds robots that clean, paint, and coat the built world. In 2025, Inc. 5000 named Lucid Bots the fastest-growing robotics manufacturer in the United States. He started it in college with a $12 soldering iron. Forbes 30 Under 30 (2020). Y Combinator S19. He served as Davidson College's Innovator-in-Residence, working with hundreds of student entrepreneurs. Personal site: https://www.andrewashur.com
